name: Roundtuit
pitch: The to-do list for jobs you'll get to eventually.
lead: The to-do list for jobs you'll get to eventually. Keep your own list, share one with the people you live with, and let them ask you for things. Eventually you'll get a roundtuit.
features: Sort jobs into categories like Home, Garden or Errands, then add your own. Each task can carry a due date, notes, cost and time spent.
Set a task to repeat at custom intervals (weekly, monthly, on a specific date and more), and a fresh copy shows up on its day. Unfinished copies stay on the list, so nothing quietly disappears.
Any task with a due date can remind you at the time you choose, and a reminder goes away once the task is done.
Share a list with the people you live with, and everyone sees the same jobs and who checked them off. Each person uses their own phone and their own account.
Give someone the right to ask you for things. Their requests land on your list in the category you picked, and they can see when each one is done.
The Metrics tab adds up what you've added and finished, plus the cost and time spent, by category, list or person.
plans: The whole list on your phone, with no ads and no account.
A backup to your own Google Drive every day, and whenever you ask.
Use Roundtuit on your phone and tablet alike, with your list in step between them.
Make lists you share, and invite people to ask you for things.
Connect your own AI app, so you can talk to it about your list, and it makes changes only when you say so.
data: Your tasks and categories are kept on your phone. If you turn on Daily Backup, a copy goes to your own Google Drive.
If you choose Sync, your list is kept in Roundtuit's online database so it follows you to a new phone and your devices all match. There are no ads, analytics or tracking.
